# My plan for this year

Alright, let me think through this. I've got 4.1 mu to work with, which isn't much for a family of seven, but the wheat and maize keep us in grain and the cotton brings in some cash. My wife and I handle most of the field work — my older brother works construction in the city and sends money home, and two of the kids are still in school, so they can only help on weekends and during summer break when we pick cotton.

I'll keep my plots about the same as last year. **Around 2.5 mu in the wheat-maize double crop** on the better ground near the canal road, and **1.6 mu in cotton** on the strip further out where the soil is a bit sandier — cotton does okay there and I don't want to fight with water timing for maize on that piece.

## Wheat (winter wheat, 2.5 mu)

I'll plant around October 10-15, same as always. I use the regular semi-dwarf variety from the seed shop — Jimai something, whatever they have. No point paying extra for a fancy one on such a small plot. Plant at around 15 kg seed per mu, a bit heavier because I direct-drill with a small rented planter and some seed gets lost.

For fertilizer, I put down a 15-15-15 compound before planting, about 40 kg per mu, then topdress urea at jointing in early March — maybe 15 kg per mu of urea if the wheat looks a bit yellow, less if it's already dark green. So total N works out to roughly 13 kg per mu from the compound plus another 7 from urea — call it 20 kg N per mu. The extension guy at the township says 15 is enough, but honestly I've seen better heads when I push it a little more, and urea isn't that expensive.

Irrigation: I'll water once before winter freeze-up if it's been dry, once at jointing, and once at heading/grain-fill. Three times usually. Each time costs me diesel and my time on the pump. If it rains well I skip the overwinter one.

Spray herbicide once in late winter for grass weeds — it's cheap and saves weeding labor I don't have. Maybe one fungicide pass at heading if I see stripe rust starting in the neighbor's field.

Yield I'm hoping for about 450 kg/mu. Last year I got 430, the year before 470. If the spring isn't too dry, 450 is realistic.

## Maize (summer maize, 2.5 mu, after wheat)

Right after I cut the wheat in early June I have to move fast — maybe 5-7 days to get the maize in. I don't plow, I just direct-seed into the wheat stubble with a borrowed no-till planter. A neighbor has the machine and I give him 15 yuan per mu. This is the only way to make the calendar work.

I use Zhengdan 958 or whatever similar hybrid the shop is pushing, costs around 50-60 yuan per mu for the seed. Plant about 4,000 plants per mu.

Fertilizer: I put a compound at planting through the planter — maybe 30 kg of 18-18-8 per mu — and then topdress urea at the big-trumpet stage in late July, about 20 kg per mu. That's around 5 kg N base plus 9 from the topdress, so roughly 14 kg N total. Maize is hungry but cash is tight after wheat so I don't push it more than that.

Irrigation: usually once or twice. The rains in July-August are pretty reliable, but if August is dry I water once at tasseling. I hate running the pump in August — electricity is expensive and I'd rather save it for the cotton.

Spray herbicide once after planting (atrazine + something), and one insecticide pass if I see borer damage. Yield target around 500 kg/mu.

## Cotton (1.6 mu)

Cotton is where I actually make cash, but it's also where I spend the most and sweat the most. My wife and I pick it ourselves over September and October — three or four pickings. The kids help on weekends. It's slow work.

I plant around April 20 after the soil warms up. I buy Bt hybrid seed — the kind resistant to bollworm — about 100 yuan per mu, it's a lot but without it the insecticide bills would be worse.

Before planting I put down a compound fertilizer, maybe 40 kg of 15-15-15 per mu. Then I topdress urea twice — once at squaring (around mid-June) maybe 10 kg, and once at flowering in July another 8 kg. That puts me around 16 kg N per mu total, which is about what everyone in the village does.

Irrigation: cotton needs water at flowering and boll-filling. I'll water twice, maybe three times if July-August is really dry. Furrow irrigation from my tube well.

Pesticide is the big cost. Even with Bt cotton I still spray for aphids, mirids, and spider mites — probably 4-5 sprays through the season. Herbicide once after planting before emergence. Call it around 150 yuan per mu on pesticides alone.

Yield target: 270 kg lint per mu. Last year cotton prices were decent; if they hold I should clear some real money off the 1.6 mu.

## Budget and labor

Total I'll spend somewhere around 1,900 yuan on inputs this year. My brother's remittances cover any shortfall, and I've got a little saved from last year's cotton. Family labor covers most of the work — only hired help I'll need is maybe a couple of days of picking help in peak cotton harvest if the weather turns.
